trades.headline: Sell Jayden Daniels at his peak for Jonathan Taylor's crash and a free Bryce Young
trades.summary: Daniels is pricing in a career year that carries real injury risk; Taylor's role hasn't actually shrunk as much as his price has, and Young comes along for nearly nothing.

give: Daniels is up 23% in 30 days on 20.1 ppg at 94% snaps — about as hot as his price will ever get.
His superflex ceiling is tied to rushing production, the least repeatable part of a QB's line.
get: Taylor's value is down 57% in 30 days, but Indianapolis says it isn't cutting his workload on purpose.
He's still at 75% snaps and 20 touches/game with a 3.1 red-zone looks/game average — a committee dip, not a benching.
Young is a near-free include: full-time Panthers starter signed through 2027 at a replacement-level price.
you: Taylor starts at FLEX and Young at SUPER_FLEX, replacing DK Metcalf and Daniels in your lineup.
Fills your thin RB spot and gives you two starters instead of one.
You'll need to drop Chase McLaughlin to open the roster spot — no lineup cost since he's your kicker.
them: Schlottamore is thin at RB/QB but deep at WR/TE — they're betting Blake Corum can cover Taylor's touches.
Daniels gives them the single best player at the league's scarcest, highest-value position outright.
experts: Colts coach Shane Steichen said before Week 9 that Taylor's workload wasn't being deliberately reduced despite trade rumors.
Taylor logged under 70% of snaps for three straight weeks through Week 10, the longest such stretch of his career since 2023.

risks: If Taylor's lighter role is permanent rather than a committee dip, this looks like a bad buy within a month.

trades.headline: Flip RB depth and Stefon Diggs for Justin Jefferson's QB-discounted target share
trades.summary: Jefferson's role is still elite, just buried under bad quarterback play; Rashee Rice's target share is already trending up. Fills your thin WR spot in one move.

give: Cook is a quality back, but your roster is deep at RB — a fair price to pay for a true WR1.
Diggs (62% snaps, 22% target share) is a complementary piece, not a difference-maker, at this point.
get: Jefferson is still running an 83% snap share and a 29% target share — his 0.78 performance-vs-projection ratio is the Vikings' QB play, not him.
Rice's target share has been trending up as the season goes, and he's already up 12% in value over 30 days.
you: Jefferson starts at WR and Rice at FLEX, replacing Cook and Diggs — a clean upgrade at your weakest position.
Keeps your deep RB room intact enough to still roster Bijan Robinson and Quinshon Judkins.
them: Schlottamore is deep at WR/TE but thin at RB; Cook is a true three-down back to address that directly.
Blake Corum slides into their flex, so they're not left empty at the position they're selling from.
experts: CBS Sports' Vikings beat coverage says a win over Buffalo didn't cure Jefferson's cold spell, pinning it on Minnesota's quarterback play under Kyler Murray.
The Fantasy Footballers flagged Rice's target share as continuing to trend up as Kansas City leans on him more.

risks: If Minnesota's QB situation never stabilizes, Jefferson's name value keeps outrunning his weekly points.

trades.headline: Sell Trevor Lawrence and Tank Dell's hot streaks for a steadier Brock Purdy plus a buy-low Stevenson
trades.summary: Lawrence's touchdown rate and Dell's per-target efficiency are both running well above what their roles support; Purdy is a proven starter in his own right, and Stevenson is cheap on a committee scare that hasn't actually cost him much.

give: Lawrence is up 43% in 30 days at 19.7 ppg on 97% snaps — a stretch analysts call partly a touchdown-rate spike that historically cools.
Dell, four games into a return from his ACL/MCL injury, is producing 1.95x his projection on just a 41% snap share and 14% target share.
get: Purdy is himself a top-3 value QB this season at 97% snaps and a 1.07 performance ratio — not a discount play, a real upgrade of your floor.
Stevenson's value is down 20% in 30 days on a knee scare and a split with TreVeyon Henderson, but he's still logging 13.5 touches/game.
you: Purdy takes over at QB and Stevenson starts at FLEX, replacing Lawrence and DK Metcalf.
Locks in value from two hot streaks before either one's efficiency normalizes.
them: A 6-5 team chasing a playoff spot pays a premium for the league's hottest superflex name and a buzzy post-injury efficiency story.
Even accounting for roster fit, both pieces carry real near-term fantasy buzz that a seller can cash in on.
experts: Footballguys' season-long look at Lawrence's breakout flags his touchdown rate as a career high unlikely to repeat at this pace.
Coverage of Stevenson's knee issue and the Henderson split describes his workload as week-to-week rather than settled.

risks: Daniels-style injury risk doesn't apply here, but Lawrence's efficiency could hold up longer than expected, making this an early sell.
Purdy has an extensive injury history of his own and could miss time.

trades.headline: Move Jayden Daniels and a committee back for Dallas's clear lead back plus a cheap backup QB
trades.summary: Javonte Williams is the Cowboys' unquestioned bellcow at a 10% value discount, while Daniels — strong as he's been — still carries real injury risk this partner may be willing to absorb.

give: Daniels is up 23% in 30 days and performing at 0.99 of projection, about as good a sell window as you'll get.
Judkins (52% snaps, 10% target share) is clearly your RB3, expendable from a deep room.
get: Williams is Dallas's only real option at RB, on a three-year extension, at 73% snaps and 19.6 touches/game — down 10% in value with no change in role.
Shough is a 100%-snap starter in New Orleans, priced as a backup after a rough 30 days (-34%).
you: Williams starts at FLEX and Shough at SUPER_FLEX, replacing Judkins and Daniels.
Trims a QB you can't start two of anyway while adding a true starting back.
them: BowerRangers, already deep at QB, are selling their lead back for a QB1 ceiling — a value bet given their quarterback depth.
It leaves Judkins as their top rostered RB, so this only makes sense for a team prioritizing the swing at QB over RB stability.
experts: RotoWire's 2026 Cowboys coverage lists Williams as the clear lead back after signing a three-year, $24M extension.
Daniels' left elbow has been dislocated in each of the past two seasons, which is the real cost of selling here, not his form.

risks: Daniels re-injuring that elbow would make this look like an easy win for you in hindsight — but that's exactly the risk you're selling off.

trades.headline: Send RB depth to a seller for two WRs whose QB situations, not their routes, are the problem
trades.summary: Olave's target share is untouched, and Flowers is being discounted for a Ravens QB carousel, not a lost role. A 4-7 team should take a sure-thing back over both.

give: Cook is a fine RB2, but your roster is deep enough at the position to spend him on a thin spot.
get: Olave is running an 82% snap share and 28% target share — his price is only down 19% because New Orleans' offense as a whole has struggled.
Flowers (71% snaps, 28% target share) is priced down 35% almost entirely because Baltimore has cycled through backup quarterbacks.
you: Both start at WR, replacing Cook and DK Metcalf — a full fix of your thin receiver spot in one trade.
Addresses need directly rather than just banking surplus value.
You'll need to drop Chase McLaughlin to open the roster spot — no lineup cost since he's your kicker.
them: Charity Case is 4-7 and out of contention; they're likely punting on 2026 and selling veteran WRs for a three-down back to build around next year.
It leaves them thinner at WR in the near term, but rookie Carnell Tate takes the vacated spot and a lead RB is the safer asset for a rebuild.
experts: RotoBaller's season outlook had Olave poised for a big target share once Jordyn Tyson opened the year on IR, and that volume has held.
Coverage of Lamar Jackson's multiple missed starts this year says Flowers has kept earning targets even as the quarterback has changed.

risks: If Baltimore's QB situation never settles, Flowers' price may not recover on your timeline.

trades.headline: Trade a buried committee back and a WR4 for a buy-low Sam LaPorta
trades.summary: LaPorta's target share and snap share haven't moved; his price has fallen on an injury tag, not a lost role. He simply outscores what Judkins was giving you at FLEX.

give: Judkins (52% snaps, 16.8 touches/game) is your RB3 behind Bijan Robinson, not a lineup piece you need.
Washington is a limited-role WR4 you aren't starting.
get: LaPorta is down 26% in value over 30 days despite an 89% snap share and 18% target share — the drop tracks his questionable tag, not his role.
you: LaPorta slots straight into your FLEX in place of Judkins, an immediate points upgrade at a position you're already deep at (McBride).
Pure value-over-need: it banks a discounted TE1-caliber talent while you still have Judkins' snaps covered elsewhere.
them: Charity Case is rebuilding at 4-7 and gets a depth back (Judkins) and a WR (Washington) for a TE they can replace with Carnell Tate.
experts: LaPorta's hip and back injury history over the past two seasons has kept his price depressed even in weeks where his usage hasn't changed.

risks: If LaPorta's questionable tag turns into a multi-week absence, this value doesn't show up on your bench for a while.
